children.description: Onchnesoma — a genus of sipunculideas.

children.name: Phascolion
children.description: Phascolion — a genus of sipunculideas.

children.name: Phascolion abnorme W.Fischer, 1895
children.description: External anatomy: Hooks type III (rounded and recurved). Holdfast papillae hardened, with a U shape. Tentacular crown consists of 10-30 tentacles. Anus on the anterior end of the trunk. Internal anatomy: Ventral retractor origin anterior to dorsal retractor. Gut forms a spiral and loops. (From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler 1994)

children.name: Phascolion bogorovi Murina, 1973
children.description: External anatomy: Large, slender and black hooks (200-250 µm) type I (see Fig. 5E from Cutler and Cutler, 1985). Holdfast papillae with granular hardened deposit, and one to four “teeth” on some posterior papillae. Dark anterior end of the trunk with large and clear lemon-shaped papillae. Anus at the anterior end of the trunk. Internal anatomy: Dorsal retractor is two or three times wider than the ventral retractor. Gut has loops and coil. (From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

children.name: Phascolion caupo Hendrix, 1975
children.description: External anatomy: Introvert about the same length as the trunk. Hooks type 3 (broad based and recurved, with a round tip), 20-35 µm tall. Holdfast papillae aretall cone-shaped and dark.They are distributed sparsely as a band in the middle of the trunk (as few as 12 holdfast papillae forming the band). Small worms have transparent hooks. Tentacular crown consists of 10-15 elongate tentacles. Internal anatomy: Dorsal muscle is 5 to 7 times broader than the ventral one. Ventral muscle has two short roots just posterior to the end of nerve cord. (From Hendrix, 1975; Cutler, 1994)

children.name: Phascolion cirratum Murina, 1968
children.description: External anatomy: Trunk rugose and lacks holdfast papillae. Tentacular crown consists of numerous dendritically branched tentacles. Anus located on the anterior introvert. Internal anatomy: Retractor muscle fused as column. Contractile vessel with numerous digitiform contractile villi. (From Murina, 1968; Cutler and Cutler, 1985)

children.name: Phascolion collare Selenka & de Man, 1883
children.description:
(From Cutler 1994, Saiz Salinas 1984, Stephen & Edmonds 1972)

External anatomy

Introvert extends through the center of the anal shield and is longer than the trunk.

The tentacular crown is only a membrane with grooves, encircling the nuchal organ (Saiz Salinas, 1984).

Distal bidentate hooks are arranged in about 23 rings (Saiz Salinas, 1984).

The anal shield has a pineapple appearance, with diamond-shaped calcareous units, each one with a dark central pore, arranged neatly against its neighbors, like mosaic tiles.

The trunk is smooth and pale and may exceed 90 mm, although most specimens are between 10 to 40 mm long.

Internal anatomy

The longitudinal muscle layer is continuous in most of the trunk with weak bands along about two-thirds of the trunk in the dorsal region.

A spindle muscle arises near the anus and is attached posteriorly.

Rectal caecum is not present.

Nephridia arise posterior to the anus and extend almost to the base of the retractors. They are fixed by mesentery to the trunk wall for most of their length except at the distal extremity.

A pair of retractor muscles originates about one fifth of the trunk length from the posterior extremity.

children.name: Phascolion convestitum Sluiter, 1902
children.description:
(From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

External anatomy

Hooks with broad base, recurved and pointed (50-100 µm tall).

Holdfast papillae from large and bulbous to small and compact. Some have granular material around the border as a distinct unit, others are without hardened material, others have a smooth and slightly darker border.

Tentacular crown consists of 20-25 normal tentacles.

Anus at the anterior end of the trunk.

Internal anatomy

Dorsal retractor slightly larger than ventral .

Dorsal retractor with single origin.

Ventral muscle with two origins, which straddle the ventral nerve cord near its posterior end.

Esophagus may be connected to the dorsal retractor muscle.

Intestine in loops with few loose coils.

Short and strong fixing muscle at the posterior end of the coil, attaching it to the trunk wall between the roots of the ventral retractor muscle (this is not a spindle muscle).

children.name: Phascolion cryptum Hendrix, 1975
children.description:
(From Hendrix, 1975)

External anatomy

The tentacular crown is formed by four primary tentacles. Usually the dorsal pair is bifid and ventral pair is trifid; in the expanded anterior introvert of live specimens the tentacles appear in the shape of an “X”.

The nuchal organ is posterior to the dorsal pair of tentacles and is often obscured by them. It is cushion-shaped and divided longitudinally into pleats. In the living specimen the pleats are white and the grooves are pink or red.

The introvert can be twice the length of the trunk. The anterior end of the introvert, just behind the nuchal organ, has a very thin wall. The internal coelomic pressure expands this region forming the introvert bulb. Encircling this bulb there are as many as seven rings of auxiliary tentacles. They are stubby outpouchings of the introvert wall. Auxiliary tentacles of the first and the last rings are simple, but the tentacles from the middle rings could have two or three lobes. The collar is a thin rim of epithelium encircling the most posterior portion of the introvert bulb, which delineates the bulb from the rest of the introvert.

A region of close-set papillae begins behind the collar and continues posteriorly along the introvert onto the anterior part of the trunk. The papillae are flask-shaped and gradually increase in size from the collar (42 µm high) to the anterior part of the trunk (84 µm high).

children.name: Phascolion hedraeum Selenka & de Man, 1883
children.description:
(From Cutler 1994, Migotto a & Ditadi 1988, Stephen & Edmonds 1972)

External anatomy

Introvert is three to five times the trunk length, without hooks, but with many cylindrical papillae (6.5-8.0µm tall), arranged in irregular rings.

Apparently this species has no tentacles.

Trunk may be up to 45 mm long, slender with a smooth white appearance.

The anal shield is composed of fine grains with small furrows around the margin and lacks grooves. A dorsoventral median line of darker units is often present.

The caudal shield is conical; radial grooves are indistinct.

Internal anatomy

The longitudinal muscle layer of the trunk wall is continuous, except under the anal shield.

Intestine attached anteriorly and posteriorly by spindle muscle.

A small rectal caecum was observed in the specimens from Brazil (Migotto & Ditadi 1988).

Nephridia are 50-70% of the trunk length, attached to the body wall and open at the same level or posteriorly to the anus.

A pair of retractor muscles rises close to the caudal shield on the posterior end of the trunk.

children.name: Phascolion hibridum Murina, 1981
children.description: External anatomy: Hooks type II with broad base (40 µm tall), and pale. Mid-trunk is smooth, lacks holdfast papillae. Dark papillae on the anterior trunk are large, mammiform, single tipped, giving the false impression of a shield. Internal anatomy: Retractor muscles with unequal size, the dorsal is larger than the ventral retractor and incompletely fused. (From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994).

children.name: Phascolion hupferi W.Fischer, 1895
children.description:
(From Stephen and Edmonds, 1972; Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

External anatomy

Introvert long, 1.5 to 4 times the trunk length.

Holdfast papillae are absent.

Hooks have not been reported.

Anus located on the introvert, about 50-75% of the distance towards the mouth

Tentacular crown consists often of more than 12 tentacles.

Internal anatomy

Retractor column fused but some specimens showtwo retractor origins, represented by a small cleft at the base.

children.name: Phascolion lucifugax Selenka & de Man, 1883
children.description:
(From Stephen and Edmonds, 1972; Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler 1994)

External anatomy

Hooks are medium sized (65-70 µm tall), type III with blunt apical extremity.

Holdfast papillae spherical without hardened border.

Tentacular crown consists of more than 30 long and slender tentacles.

Internal anatomy

Retractor muscles with same diameter (1.5 mm broad), attach about 15% of the distance from the posterior end of the trunk. Origin of the ventral retractor muscle is slightly divided and is posterior to origin of the dorsal retractor muscle.

Esophagus attached to the ventral retractor muscles, bearing a large vesicular contractile vessel.

Intestine with loops, no coils.

children.name: Phascolion lutense Selenka, 1885
children.description:
(From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

External anatomy

Hooks type I (40-150 µm tall), sparsely distributed, but some specimens lack hooks.

Trunk smooth with small, densely packed papillae at the anterior end. Mid-trunk with inconspicuous skin bodies.

Holdfast papillae completely absent.

Tentacular crown described by Selenka (1895) consists of a few short tentacles (16 at most). Cutler and Cutler (1985) described specimens with extended introverts as having a continuous folded membrane, possibly with several lobes, surrounding the mouth.

Internal anatomy

Retractor muscles fused for most of their length, but 3 or 4 short roots may be present.

children.name: Phascolion manceps Selenka, de Man & Bülow, 1883
Phascolion medusae E.Cutler & Cutler, 1980
children.description: External anatomy: Introvert is equal in length to the trunk. Hooks type III, 50 µm tall. Tentacular crown has about 50 filamentous tentacles. Holdfast papillae are large, mushroom or wart shaped, without distinct borders. Internal anatomy: Dorsal retractor muscles originate posterior to the ventral. Esophagus attached for most of the length of the ventral retractor muscle. Gut lacks coils. Contractile vessel is vesicular. Anus anterior to the nephridiopores. (From Cutler and Cutler 1980, Cutler, 1994).

children.name: Phascolion megaethi E.Cutler & Cutler, 1980
children.description: External anatomy: Trunk smooth, with a few small V-shaped holdfast papillae at the posterior tip. Few blunt hooks type III, 30-35 µm tall. Papillae from the anterior end of the trunk, mammiform, dark red, 100-150 µm tall, giving a false impression of a shieldlike array. Tentacular crown with fewer than 15 tentacles. Internal anatomy: Ventral retractor muscle (fused single root) originates posterior to the large dorsal retractor (single root). Gut lacks coils. (Cutler and Cutler, 1979; Cutler, 1994).

children.name: Phascolion pacificum Murina, 1957
children.description:
(From Murina, 1957; Cutler and Cutler, 1985, Cutler, 1994).

External anatomy

Introvert equal in length to trunk.

Trunk length 1-19 mm.

Hooks type I, small and pale.

Holdfast papillae with U or V shape and a thin hardened border.

Papillae from the anterior end of the trunk are mammiform or conical. Interpapillar space packed with mud.

Tentacular crown consists of reduced lobes (specimens from Japan and Bay of Biscay).

Internal anatomy

Retractor column usually fused for most of its length with 2 to 4 roots at the base but extent of fusion is variable.

Esophagus detached from the retractor column before any split.

children.name: Phascolion pharetratum Sluiter, 1902
children.description: External anatomy: Hooks type II, bent, dull, and dark brown. Holdfast papillae absent. Tentacular crown consists of filamentous tentacles. Internal anatomy: Introvert retractor muscles originate well anterior to the posterior end of the trunk. Gut has a regular spiral. (From Stephen and Edmonds; 1972, Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

children.name: Phascolion psammophilum Rice, 1993
children.description: External anatomy: Introvert 1-2.4 times the trunk length (average 1.7 mm). Trunk commonly about 2 mm long. Hooks type II, bluntly pointed, 30 µm tall (small for this genus), in one to four irregular rings. Nuchal organ on the dorsal tip of the introvert. Holdfast papillae absent. Some trunk papillae have a knob or a cap apex, others have one to three apical pores. Tentacular crown having 2 to 8 elongate tentacles. Anus on the introvert, about 20% of the distance towards the tip. Internal anatomy: Retractor muscles originate at the same level very close to the posterior end of the trunk. Gut is not coiled and is attached to the trunk wall by a few fixing muscles. Rectum long with a caecum at its beginning.Small glandular sacs just in front of the nephridiopores open to the exterior via pores. (From Rice, 1993)

children.name: Phascolion rectum Ikeda, 1904
children.description:
(From Cutler and Cutler, 1981; Cutler 1994)

External anatomy

Introvert about 1.5 times the trunk length.

Hooks and holdfast papillae are absent.

Anus located on the anterior trunk.

Internal anatomy

Gut has a short spiral and loose loops.

Tentacular crown with less than 12 tentacles.

Nephridium opening just posterior to the anus and free from the trunk wall.

children.name: Phascolion robertsoni Stephen & Robertson, 1952
children.description: External anatomy: Hooks type III, 30-40 µm tall. Holdfast papillae, 100-200 µm wide, scattered, pale, U or V shaped, and associated with large, bulbous papillae. Papillae, pale, and dark, hardened tips around the base part of the introvert. Tentacular crown consists of 40 slender tentacles. Internal anatomy: Dorsal retractor muscle three times larger than the ventral retractor, originates at the posterior end of the trunk, slightly (few millimeters) anterior to the ventral. Gut has only loops. Nephridiopores posterior to the anus. (From Stephen and Edmonds, 1972; Cutler and Cutler, 1985)

children.name: Phascolion tuberculosum Théel, 1875
children.description:
(From Cutler and Cutler, 1985; Cutler, 1994)

External anatomy

Hooks, large (70-220 µm tall) broad, recurved (type II).

Holdfast papillae, large (80-330 µm in diameter) spherical, lackinga chitinous border. Occasionally some granular material may accumulate along the anterior margin.

Papillae around the anterior part of the trunk are mammiform, usually with one tip, but two to four tips have been observed.

Tentacular crown consists of 15 stumpy tentacles.

Internal anatomy

Retractor muscles occasionally differ from one another in diameter by 25%. They originate close to the posterior end of the trunk, attached at nearly the same level. Ventral retractor muscle occasionally is attached 1-2 mm anterior to the dorsal retractor.

children.name: Phascolion ushakovi Murina, 1974
children.description: External anatomy: Hooks type I, black, spinelike. Middle trunk with flattened skin bodies instead of holdfast papillae. Large mammiform papillae on both ends of the trunk. Internal anatomy: Thin ventral retractor muscle one-fifth to one-tenth the size of the dorsal retractor. Gut coils attached by several fixing muscles to the trunk wall, with a posterior one of large diameter (it is not a spindle muscle). (From Cutler and Cutler, 1985)
